summary.headline: Flair Writing Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8.4% to INR322.9 crore, FY26 revenue up 15.8% to INR1,250.1 crore; crude-linked raw material costs now a margin headwind in Q1 FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 15.8% to INR1,250.1 crore, meeting the company's 15% guidance, with EBITDA up 21.5% to INR224.5 crore and EBITDA margin up 85 bps to 18%. Q4 revenue grew 8.4% to INR322.9 crore, with gross margin up 258 bps to 51.2% and EBITDA margin up 217 bps to 17.9%. Own-brand sales reached 91% of revenue, while OEM sales fell, and Creative and Steel Bottles & Houseware together reached 31% of revenue. Management flagged that crude-derivative raw material costs (about 35% of raw materials) rose sharply due to the West Asia crisis, with an expected ~4% margin hit in Q1 FY27 and ~1% by year-end, and retained 15% FY27 revenue guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Debtors -4 days QoQ; creditors -3 days QoQ

segments.name: Own brand (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 domestic own-brand sales INR264 crore, +17% YoY; FY26 INR1,017 crore, +20%. Own-brand exports Q4 INR34 crore (+31%), FY26 INR122 crore (+29%).

segments.name: OEM
segments.commentary: Domestic OEM fell from INR15 crore to INR9 crore in Q4; legacy domestic OEM at zero, with new Flomaxe-subsidiary engagements. Export OEM fell from INR32 crore to INR17 crore in Q4 on subdued client demand and West Asia disruption.

segments.name: Creative
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR86 crore, +80% YoY; FY26 INR298 crore, +74%. 29 new products in FY26 and six in Q4. Wooden pencil manufacturing started at Flomaxe Surat facility.

segments.name: Steel Bottles & Houseware
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR22 crore, +76% YoY (from INR12 crore); FY26 INR85 crore, +95%. 24 products; growth levers are portfolio expansion and general trade distribution.

segments.name: Pens
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR213.4 crore, -4% YoY (from INR221.7 crore), driven by Pen OEM down 65%; Pen own-brand grew 9%. Own brand now 95% of Pens revenue vs 80% a year ago.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% maintained despite West Asia crisis; management targets Pens ~5%, Creative ~50%, Steel Bottles ~40%.
Q1 FY27 margin impact: raw material cost inflation of ~13% weighted average on consumption, net ~4% margin impact in Q1, narrowing over the next three quarters to ~1% by end FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin target around 18%, with a possible swing of about 1% either way (management cited a 17%-19% range when asked).
Mitigation via scheme and discount rationalisation and selling price increases in household and steelware, plus premiumisation.
Inventory days expected to fall 5-7 days over the next two quarters as pre-stocking was a one-time event; working capital impact of ~9 days expected going forward.
Final dividend of INR0.50 per share (10% of face value), 20% of FY26 face value, same as prior year.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR104 crore, of which INR40 crore in Q4; INR20 crore spent on Flomaxe Surat facility (building and plant & machinery).
Valsad facility operations to commence Q1 FY27, with capacity ramp-up by Q3 FY27; Q4 start was reported as slightly delayed due to machinery and raw material delays.
FY27 capex expected at INR80-90 crore, including INR60-70 crore for Valsad; annual replacement capex around INR42 crore.
Management cites ~3x asset turnover; peak achievable sales from current and planned assets estimated at ~INR1,750 crore.
Plans to add a fourth steel bottle line; no asset-light model planned.
demand_pricing: Back-to-school demand described as very positive with no dent after price increases, per management.

Raw material mix: crude-linked derivatives ~35% of raw materials; weighted average input inflation ~13% (range 0% to 50% across items). About 4-5 weeks of raw and packing stock built up, representing ~40% of inventory.
Middle East exports ~25% of total export revenue; shipments to the region paused for past couple of months due to route closure.
Export reach is 100+ countries after four new countries were added.

Creative growth to come from pencils (mechanical, wooden, 2mm) and kids categories, plus geometry boxes and colouring range; growth expected to come from taking share from existing players rather than adding outlets.
Creative touch points ~65,000-70,000 outlets; management plans to deepen throughput per outlet rather than add outlets.
Receivable improvement attributed to collection process changes; management expects further improvement as Steel, Household and Creative grow.

qa_highlights.question: How much of raw material is crude-linked, how much price hike has been taken, and was there channel stocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude derivatives are about 35% of raw materials; weighted input inflation is ~13%. Pre-stocking was done by buying at dips, which dampens the cost increase. Price hikes taken in household and steelware; schemes being rationalised.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Pens given it grew ~2% vs high-single-digit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets ~5% annual Pens growth, ~50% for Creative and ~40% for Steel Bottles, with overall growth around 15% and mix of Creative and Steel rising to ~15% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steel bottle revenue moderate QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 benefited from festive season; company is strengthening general trade, modern trade and e-commerce/quick commerce and launching new ranges.

qa_highlights.question: Margin impact and normalisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Maximum ~4% impact in Q1 FY27, easing over three quarters to ~1% by year-end FY27; longer if conflict persists, with pricing actions needed to pass through costs.

qa_highlights.question: Peak revenue potential from existing and planned capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR1,750 crore of sales from the facilities being built, including Valsad; asset-light model not under consideration.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone operating profit flat/declining while consolidated grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Machinery is fungible across entities; product allocation across Daman, Valsad, Dehradun and Surat drives standalone vs subsidiary profit. Management points to consolidated numbers as the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost trend versus gross profit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost plus job work is 20-21% of consolidated revenue and stable; other expenses declining as a percentage of sales.

risks_watch: Crude-linked raw material inflation (~35% of raw materials) could extend the margin hit beyond the ~4% Q1 estimate if the West Asia conflict persists.
Valsad facility started late relative to earlier guidance; ramp-up by Q3 FY27 needs monitoring.
Middle East export route closures (about 25% of exports) and weak export OEM demand (down ~47% YoY in Q4).
Inventory days at 97 in Q4 versus 87 in FY25; management targets a 5-7 day reduction over two quarters.
Standalone operating profit trend (Pens-led entity) has lagged revenue growth; employee cost is a fixed-cost lever.
Pens revenue growth of ~2% in FY26 versus high-single-digit earlier guidance; new 5% target to be tracked.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year growth outlook and maintaining 15% guidance, but cautious on near-term margins, with repeated caveats that the West Asia crisis outcome is uncertain. Some answers on standalone profitability and Pens were defensive or indirect.

As mentioned in our previous calls that we are seeing operating leverage come through this year.
So the demand is extremely positive when we talk about the back -to-school season.

adds.what: Valsad facility (operations to commence Q1 FY27, ramp-up by Q3 FY27), INR60-70 crore FY27 capex
Fourth steel bottle line (planned, no timing or capex given)

growth.why: Management held FY27 revenue growth guidance at 15% (FY26 delivered 15.8%), backed by Valsad capacity starting Q1 FY27 with ramp by Q3 FY27, 29 new products in FY26, price increases and export reach, though no order book or quantified capacity-to-revenue bridge was given and West Asia crude cost inflation is a margin headwind.
